meta.name: South America
meta.description: All South American STEM & Physics institutions, Andean astronomical observatories, national labs, and regional milestones.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

hubs.name: ESO Paranal Observatory
hubs.summary: Four giant 8.2 m mirror domes perched atop a Martian-red Andean peak—the sharpest optical eyes on Earth.
hubs.nobel: Reinhard Genzel (2020 Nobel) tracked stars whipping around the Milky Way's central black hole here.

stages.highschool: ESO Astronomy Camp in the Italian Alps & open VLT archive imagery.
stages.undergrad: ESO Summer Research Programme (6-week paid astrophysics stay in Garching).
stages.masters: ESO Studentships (1–2 years in Chile or Germany during MSc/PhD).
stages.phd: IMPRS Astrophysics / ESO Studentships observing directly on the VLT.
stages.postdoc: ESO Fellowship (3–4 years in Chile or Garching with 25% observatory duties).
stages.assoc_prof: ESO Staff Astronomer & VLT/ELT instrument PI.
stages.prof: ESO Director for Science & Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) leadership.

hubs.name: ICTP-SAIFR
hubs.summary: Latin America's vibrant partner to ICTP Trieste, hosting free international schools in cosmology and theoretical physics.
hubs.nobel: Connected directly with ICTP Trieste, Perimeter Institute, and Fermilab.

stages.highschool: ICTP-SAIFR High School Physics Minicourses & outreach.
stages.undergrad: Free intensive Journeys into Theoretical Physics for Latin American undergrads.
stages.masters: FAPESP-funded Master's fellowships in Theoretical Physics at IFT-UNESP.
stages.phd: FAPESP funded PhD with international travel grants to ICTP & Perimeter.
stages.postdoc: ICTP-SAIFR / FAPESP 2–3 year theoretical physics postdocs.

projects.name: South American Cosmology & Fundamental Physics Schools

hubs.name: ALMA Radio Observatory
hubs.summary: 66 high-precision radio antennas at 5,000 m altitude in the Atacama Desert—key anchor of the Event Horizon Telescope black-hole image.
hubs.nobel: Co-imaged the M87* and Sagittarius A* supermassive black hole shadows.

stages.highschool: ALMA Kids & open millimeter-wave astronomy data explorers.
stages.undergrad: NRAO / ESO summer student programs working on ALMA interferometry.
stages.masters: MSc projects via ESO, NAOJ, NRAO, or Chilean university partners.
stages.phd: Joint international PhDs analyzing ALMA protoplanetary disks and black holes.
stages.postdoc: ALMA / ESO / NAOJ / NRAO Fellowships in Santiago, Garching, or Charlottesville.
stages.assoc_prof: ALMA Regional Center (ARC) scientist & Large Program PI.

hubs.name: UdelaR Instituto de Física
hubs.summary: Uruguay's flagship public physics center (Facultad de Ciencias & Ingeniería), globally recognized for loop quantum gravity, nonlinear optics, and biophysics.
hubs.nobel: Home to Rodolfo Gambini's pioneering contributions to loop quantum gravity and canonical relativity.

stages.highschool: Olimpiada Uruguaya de Física & open university science outreach.
stages.undergrad: Tuition-free Licenciatura en Física with early lab integration.
stages.masters: PEDECIBA Física Master's program with national ANII scholarships.
stages.phd: PEDECIBA / ANII funded PhD in Quantum Gravity, Optics, or Condensed Matter.
stages.postdoc: ANII & ICTP-SAIFR regional postdoctoral mobility grants.
stages.assoc_prof: Profesor Agregado (Grado 4) in Facultad de Ciencias / Ingeniería.

projects.name: PEDECIBA Physics & Quantum Gravity Research Program

hubs.name: Pierre Auger Observatory
hubs.summary: The world's largest cosmic-ray observatory—spanning 3,000 km² of the Argentine Pampa Amarilla with 1,660 water-Cherenkov detectors and 27 fluorescence telescopes.
hubs.nobel: Proved that ultra-high-energy cosmic rays above 8 EeV originate outside the Milky Way.

stages.highschool: Pierre Auger Open Data Portal & Malargüe Visitor Center.
stages.undergrad: Auger Open Data analysis projects & summer stays at partner universities.
stages.masters: MSc theses across 17 member countries (Argentina, Germany, Italy, France, USA, etc.).
stages.phd: PhD fellowships working on AugerPrime scintillator and radio-detector upgrades.
stages.postdoc: Astroparticle physics postdocs in Mendoza, Buenos Aires, KIT Karlsruhe, or INFN.
stages.assoc_prof: Collaboration Task Leader & national funding PI.
stages.prof: Pierre Auger Observatory Spokesperson & International Finance Board.

hubs.name: Las Campanas & Giant Magellan Telescope
hubs.summary: Home of the twin 6.5 m Magellan Telescopes and the construction site of the 25.4 m Giant Magellan Telescope (seven 8.4 m monolithic mirrors) under pristine Andean skies.
hubs.nobel: Site of the 1987A supernova discovery and next-generation exoplanet biosignature imaging.

stages.highschool: Carnegie Science & GMT educational astronomy portals.
stages.undergrad: Carnegie Observatories Summer Undergraduate Research Program (CASSI).
stages.masters: MSc instrumentation & astrophysics projects with GMT consortium universities.
stages.phd: PhDs at Carnegie, Harvard, Chicago, Arizona, ANU, KASI, FAPESP, or Chilean universities.
stages.postdoc: Carnegie Fellows & Las Campanas Instrumentation Fellowships.
stages.assoc_prof: GMT First-Light Instrument PI & Consortium Faculty.
stages.prof: GMTO Observatory Leadership & Science Advisory Committee.

hubs.name: IMPA (Instituto de Matemática Pura e Aplicada)
hubs.summary: Latin America's crown jewel of mathematics in the Tijuca forest of Rio de Janeiro, world-renowned for dynamical systems, differential geometry, fluid mechanics, and Brazil's 18-million-student OBMEP math olympiad.
hubs.nobel: Alumnus and Extraordinary Researcher Artur Avila won the 2014 Fields Medal—the first Fields Medalist educated entirely in Latin America.

stages.highschool: Compete in OBMEP (Brazilian Public School Math Olympiad, 18M+ students annually) run by IMPA.
stages.undergrad: IMPA Tech undergraduate degree in Mathematics of Technology and Innovation & Summer Program (Programa de Verão).
stages.masters: Fully funded IMPA MSc program drawing top mathematical talent from across South America.
stages.phd: IMPA PhD in Dynamical Systems, Algebraic Geometry, PDEs, Computer Graphics, and ML.
stages.postdoc: CAPES/CNPq and IMPA Postdoctoral Fellowships in Rio de Janeiro.
stages.assoc_prof: Permanent Research Faculty (Pesquisador) positions with strong international visitor exchanges.
stages.prof: Visiting Researcher collaborations (IMPA hosted the 2018 International Congress of Mathematicians).

rabbitLinks.reason: Partners across Brazil with São Paulo's ICTP-SAIFR to anchor South American mathematics and theoretical physics.
Fields Medalist Artur Avila holds joint appointments uniting IMPA Rio de Janeiro and University of Zurich / ETH ecosystem.

events.title: Discovery of Deep-Sea Hydrothermal Vents & Chemosynthetic Life
events.figure: Robert Ballard, Jack Corliss & WHOI Alvin Team
events.summary: Diving 2,500 meters in WHOI's submersible Alvin, oceanographers discovered volcanic seafloor vents teeming with giant tube worms thriving without sunlight via chemosynthesis.
events.impact: Proved life can flourish solely on geothermal chemistry—redefining hypotheses on the origin of life and astrobiology on Europa and Enceladus.

events.title: First Horizon-Scale Image of a Black Hole (M87*)
events.location: Global VLBI Array (anchored at ALMA, Chile)
events.summary: Linked millimeter-wave radio dishes across Earth into a planet-sized virtual telescope to resolve the glowing asymmetric photon ring around the 6.5-billion-solar-mass black hole in M87.
events.impact: Provided direct visual confirmation of strong-field general relativity at an event horizon.

events.title: Vera C. Rubin Observatory First Light & LSST Survey
events.summary: Equipped with a 3.2-gigapixel camera on an 8.4 m wide-field telescope, Rubin unveiled its First Look imagery in June 2025 and began full 10-year LSST southern-sky survey operations in July 2026 to map dark matter, dark energy, and cosmic transients.
events.impact: Creates a 10-year ultra-high-definition time-lapse movie of the universe (~20 terabytes nightly).

events.title: ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) First Light
events.summary: The world's largest optical/near-infrared telescope featuring a 39.3-meter primary mirror composed of 798 hexagonal segments—targeted for mirror installation in 2028 and technical first light in 2029 to directly image rocky exoplanets.
events.impact: Will collect 100 million times more light than the human eye, probing exoplanet biosignatures and cosmic acceleration directly.
